findings.title: By-value duckdb_result args (fetch_chunk / result_return_type / result_statement_type) are lowered via _call_lib_func_byval (func(T*) semantics), which omits the SysV x86-64 byval stack copy so the 48-byte struct is read from uninitialized stack
findings.description: ducklib.py:946, 1132, 1138 wrap three DuckDB C API functions with numbox's `_call_lib_func_byval`: duckdb_fetch_chunk, duckdb_result_return_type, duckdb_result_statement_type. Per duckdb.h 1.5.4 all three take the result struct BY VALUE, not by pointer: `duckdb_data_chunk duckdb_fetch_chunk(duckdb_result result)` (L4640), `duckdb_result_type duckdb_result_return_type(duckdb_result result)` (L1136), `duckdb_statement_type duckdb_result_statement_type(duckdb_result result)` (L974). `duckdb_result` is a real 6-field struct (3x idx_t + 3 pointers) = 48 bytes; numbduck models it as `duckdb_result_ty = UniTuple(intp, 6)` (ducklib.py:68), an ABI-LARGE (>16B) aggregate. `_call_lib_func_byval` / `_emit_byval_call` (numbox call.py:280-301, 203-209) is explicitly documented as the lowering for C signatures of the form `func(T*)` (a genuine pointer parameter): it does alloca + store + call-through-pointer with NO `byval` attribute and NO `optnone`/`noinline`. That lowering does not match a `func(T)` by-value 48-byte struct on SysV x86-64. On SysV x86-64 a 48-byte struct is MEMORY class and is passed INLINE ON THE STACK (the caller copies the bytes into the outgoing argument area; the callee reads them there). Verified by disassembly: a callee compiled from a 48-byte by-value signature reads its argument with `mov 0x30(%rsp),%rax` (from the stack), whereas the pointer form reads `mov 0x28(%rdi),%rax` (through the register). `_call_lib_func_byval` instead passes only the alloca pointer in RDI and never populates the outgoing stack argument area, so the real callee reads its 48-byte `result` from uninitialized/stale stack memory. An isolated mismatched-pointer call to such a callee returns pure garbage at -O0 (returned a stack address, not the struct field) and returns the correct value at -O2 only by coincidence (the caller's copy happened to land where the callee reads). numbox's own `_call_lib_func` LARGE-arg path handles exactly this size class correctly: it adds `byval` + `optnone` + `noinline` ONLY on SysV x86-64 (call.py:170-171, 185-189) and passes a plain pointer on Windows x64 / AAPCS64 (where the ABI genuinely passes >16B aggregates by reference). So `_call_lib_func_byval` is ABI-correct for these three functions on Windows x64 and ARM64 but ABI-incorrect on SysV x86-64, where it works today only by stack-layout coincidence.
findings.impact: On Linux x86-64 (the primary CI/target platform) the three calls currently return correct results only because numba's JIT stack layout happens to place the alloca'd copy where the by-value callee reads. This is not guaranteed: a numba/LLVM version bump, a change to NUMBDUCK_JIT_OPTIONS (e.g. disabling inline or a different optimization level), or altered surrounding stack usage can silently move the read off the copy. Failure is silent and severe: duckdb_result_return_type / duckdb_result_statement_type would return a wrong enum, and duckdb_fetch_chunk would read a garbage `internal_data` pointer (offset 40 of the struct) that DuckDB then dereferences to locate the result set -> wild-pointer read / segfault / UB. duckdb_fetch_chunk is the central result-fetch primitive used throughout the test suite and downstream code, so the blast radius is the whole read path. Because the byval copy is exact-sized (48B alloca == struct), this is not an out-of-bounds write, but it is an ABI-incorrect read of the wrong 48 bytes of stack.
findings.recommendation: Route all three by-value functions through numbox's `_call_lib_func` (the ABI-aware by-value large-struct path) instead of `_call_lib_func_byval`. E.g. `return _call_lib_func("duckdb_fetch_chunk", (duckdb_result,))` and likewise `_call_lib_func("duckdb_result_return_type", (result,))` / `_call_lib_func("duckdb_result_statement_type", (result,))`. The registered signatures are already `intp(duckdb_result_ty)` / `int32(duckdb_result_ty)` (ducklib.py:172, 224, 225), so no signature change is needed: `_classify` sees the 48-byte UniTuple as STRUCT_LARGE and applies `byval`+`optnone`+`noinline` on SysV x86-64 (correct inline stack copy) and a plain pointer on Windows x64 / AAPCS64 (correct by-reference) -- ABI-correct on every supported platform. Reserve `_call_lib_func_byval` for genuine `func(T*)` parameters (it is currently used for nothing else in ducklib.py). Lock the fix with a round-trip test that fetches a chunk and validates column data with inlining disabled / low opt, to defeat the current coincidence.

notes: Scope: MEM/ABI audit of the by-value marshalling path -- the _call_lib_func_byval callers (duckdb_fetch_chunk ducklib.py:946, duckdb_result_return_type :1132, duckdb_result_statement_type :1138) and the struct-in bind wrappers at EOF (duckdb_bind_hugeint/_uhugeint/_interval/_decimal :1411-1432), read against numbox call.py/abi.py (numbox 0.5.23) and duckdb.h 1.5.4. Buffer sizing was checked and is sound everywhere: _emit_byval_call allocas exactly the struct size (48B for duckdb_result); the 16B hugeint/uhugeint (canonical {i64,i64}) and 16B interval ({i32,i32,i64}, INT/INT repack to {i64,i64}) and 24B decimal (LARGE, byval on SysV) all go through _call_lib_func with correct size/alignment and the correct per-platform ABI (verified via _basetuple_layout vs the duckdb.h layouts). The only defect is the intrinsic-selection mismatch in DCK-byval-MEM-1: three by-value (func(T)) functions are lowered with the func(T*) intrinsic, which drops the SysV x86-64 byval inline-stack-copy. Confirmed by C disassembly (by-value callee reads mov 0x30(%rsp); pointer callee reads mov 0x28(%rdi)) and an isolated mismatched-pointer call returning garbage at -O0. The finding is currently masked (green CI, strong value-asserting tests e.g. test_ducklib.py aux_get_data_vector), i.e. it is a latent ABI-correctness/memory-safety defect, not an active failure -- reported HIGH for silent-corruption potential on the primary platform with a trivial, numbox-blessed fix. Signature fidelity (arg/return types) is out of scope here and covered by DCK-sig-COR.
